label: piano
note: One pianist, two hands; MARC 382 $a piano $n 1

label: piano
note: Two or more pianists or pianos (4 hands, 2 pianos); LCMPT records the count in MARC 382 $n, not a separate term

label: keyboard instrument
note: Harpsichord, clavichord, celesta, harmonium and similar; the LCMPT term also covers piano and organ
One instrument, alone or with one keyboard; no LC term for the grouping, the LCMPT term is the instrument named in the IMSLP For … category

label: lute
note: Also archlute, theorbo and vihuela

label: plucked string instrument
note: The LCMPT term also covers harp

label: Chamber music
note: Two or more instrumentalists; LCGFT also uses the term for vocal chamber music

label: Concertos
note: Soloist(s) with orchestra or string orchestra

label: voice
note: Solo voice(s) with any accompaniment

label: Songs
note: The family also holds arias

label: chorus
note: Any chorus, or three or more unaccompanied voices

label: Operas
note: LCGFT folds Singspiels into Operas

label: Musicals
note: LCGFT folds Operettas into Musicals

label: Motion picture music
note: IMSLP film categories

label: Incidental music
note: IMSLP incidental-music categories

label: Radio music
note: IMSLP radio categories

label: electronics
note: LCGFT has no medium-based term for electronic music; tape and computer parts count here

label: Studies (Music)
note: IMSLP Etudes, Studies, Exercises

label: Methods (Music)
note: IMSLP Methods
Residual: categories that name no force; no LC equivalent

label: Chamber music
note: LCGFT has no medium-based term; catalogues add LCMPT violin (2), viola, cello. The value also fires on IMSLP Quartets, i.e. any quartet

label: Songs
note: IMSLP Songs or Lieder that are not song cycles; the LCGFT term also covers song cycles
